title: Pastel Colors
content: Apply soft pastel palette with gentle, desaturated colors - pink-200, blue-200, mint green (emerald-200), lavender (violet-200), peach (orange-200). Use white or cream backgrounds (bg-white or bg-orange-50). Add very subtle shadows (shadow-sm) with colored tints. Keep typography clean and readable against light backgrounds. Use gentle gradients between pastel colors. Include rounded corners for soft appearance. Create a calm, soothing visual experience. Balance multiple pastels without overwhelming - use one dominant color with accents.

variants.simple: Apply soft, gentle pastel colors for a calm and soothing appearance.

variants.advanced: Apply soft pastel palette with gentle, desaturated colors - pink-200, blue-200, mint green (emerald-200), lavender (violet-200), peach (orange-200). Use white or cream backgrounds (bg-white or bg-orange-50/50). Add very subtle shadows (shadow-sm) with colored tints matching nearby elements. Keep typography clean and readable - use gray-700 or gray-800 for text to ensure contrast against light pastels. Use gentle gradients between analogous pastel colors for smooth transitions. Include generous rounded corners (rounded-xl to rounded-2xl) for soft appearance. Create calm, soothing visual experience appropriate for wellness, children, or lifestyle apps. Balance multiple pastels using 60-30-10 rule - one dominant pastel, one secondary, accent sparingly. IMPORTANT: Pastel-on-pastel combinations often fail accessibility - always verify contrast ratios. Use darker text colors, not pastel text. Ensure interactive elements have sufficient visual weight to be identifiable. Add subtle borders (border-gray-200) where pastel backgrounds meet. Consider users with low vision who may struggle with low-contrast pastel interfaces.
